content: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is generally diagnosed when fasting blood glucose levels fall within the range of 110-125 mg/dL (6.1-6.9 mmol/L). Additionally, an A1C level of 5.9% (41 mmol/mol) can also indicate the presence of GDM. To confirm the diagnosis of GDM, screening methods such as the Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) are commonly employed. Specifically, the 75-gram OGTT is a widely accepted and utilized test for this purpose. The International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) has established standardized diagnostic criteria for GDM. These criteria include specific glucose level thresholds that must be met during the OGTT to confirm the diagnosis.
